sentences.text:
The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage of accused No.1 and deceased Smt.Piyali Mukerjee was performed on 05.02.2021 at Pune, Maharashtra State.
After marriage, the deceased and accused No.1 were started their marital life at Plot No.201, situated at 'A' block, Shradda Palamera Apartment, Kaverappa Layout, Marathahalli, Bengaluru.

Such being the case, after sometime, the accused not leading marital life with the deceased by keeping extra marital relationship with another woman and also not responding to the messages, phone calls of the deceased and thereby accused emotionally and mentally tortured the deceased, due to which on 24.02.2023, the deceased at her matrimonial house committed suicide leaving behind the death note and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
3.
The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.

The same was numbered as SC No.859/2023.
4.
The prosecution has examined fourteen witnesses as PW.1 to PW.14 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P21 and M.Os.1 and 2.
On consent of the accused counsel, the P.M.Report has been marked at Ex.P.11.
As such the learned PP gave up the witnesses C.W.12, 14, 15, 17 and 18.
The witnesses C.W.2 and C.W.10 cited in the charge sheet are one and the same.

5. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused,
as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.
The following points that arises for consideration of this court:

1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 and deceased-Smt.Piyali Mukerjee are being the husband and wife, the accused subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty by keeping extra marital relationship with another woman and also not responding to the messages, phone calls of the deceased and abusing her in filthy language and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 498A of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused No.1 and deceased-Smt.Piyali Mukerjee are being the husband and wife, subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty, accused emotionally and mentally tortured to the deceased, due to which on 24.02.2023 the deceased at her matrimonial house committed suicide leaving behind Marathahalli P.S vs A1 Mayukh Mukherjee on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165624995/
2 the death note and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.306 of IPC?
3. What order?

sentences.text:
8. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9. Points Nos.1 and 2: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

It is the specific allegations against the accused that he has tortured the victim emotionally and mentally by not receiving her phone call and not replying the message, as he had extra marital relationship with other woman.
Due to such torture received by the deceased, has lost her desire to lead marital life with accused and after writing the death note, committed suicide at her matrimonial house on 24.02.2023.
As we know very well that the burden is on the prosecution to establish the guilt against the accused.
To prove the said allegation, the prosecution has succeeded to examine 14 witnesses as PW.1 to P.W.14.

Among the said 14 witnesses, the witness C.W.1/P.W.1 Pronab Kumar Sharma being the father of the deceased has categorically deposed about the marriage between the accused and victim on 05.02.2021 at Pune according to the Hindu customs.
After marriage, they were residing together for 11 months at Pune.
Thereafter both were transferred to Bengaluru.
According to the complainant, there were no misunderstanding between the accused and the victim, and the victim was serving as Engineer in Amazon company and attending her work from home.
The said witness does not know the reasons for committing suicide by his daughter Piyali Mukerjee.
According to him, he has never see the video recorded by the victim before her death nor he does not know anything about the death note.
Even though the complaint and spot Mahazar marked at Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, but according to the version of the complainant, nothing has been seized while conducting the Mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
He has identified the marriage invitation and photos of accused and victim marked at Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4.
The pen-drive has been marked at Ex.P.5.
The diary has been shown to the complainant marked at QD1 to D15 present in Bengali language, but the said witness not identified the handwriting of the victim/deceased.

After receiving the phone on 24.02.2023 at 4.00 p.m about death of his daughter, immediately he has travelled to Bengaluru and saw the dead body at C.V.Raman hospital, after collecting the dead body returned to his native and carried out funeral ceremony.
Since the evidence of P.W.1 not in favour of the prosecution, hence, the learned PP has treated the witness as hostile and cross-examined by suggesting the contents of complaint and Mahazar.
Unfortunately, the father of the deceased not accepted the suggestions of the learned PP and thereby not supported the prosecution story.
As such, the evidence given by the father of the deceased not helpful for the prosecution in any manner.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the witness P.W.2 Prabhata Kumar Rat, P.W.9 Biswajita Das being the signatories to the Mahazar Ex.P.2 failed to support the conducting of Mahazar by the Investigation Officer and seizure of diary and mobile belongs to the deceased.
The both witnesses failed to identify the seized M.Os i.e. diary and mobile alleged to be seized under Mahazar marked at Ex.P.2.

So also,
the witness P.W.9 not supported his statement alleged to be given before the Investigation Officer with regard to Ex.P.2.
As such, this statement has been marked at Ex.P.13.

Whereas the P.W.2 Mr.Prabhata Kumar Rat and P.W.6 Tejas H.Pandit though identified their signatures present on the seizure Mahazar Ex.P.6, but not supported the prosecution story by deposing iota evidence.

As such,
the evidence given by the witnesses P.W.2, P.W.6 and P.W.9 not helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.

11. It is pertinent to note that the witnesses P.W.3 Shalini, P.W.5 Saket Suman and PW.7 Padam Kanwar Bhati being the signatories to the Inquest Mahazar marked at Ex.P.7 not completely aware about the contents of Ex.P.7.

It is the say of P.W.5 that the deceased is the sister of her friend, she has never met deceased Piyali Mukerjee though they identified their signatures present on Ex.P.7,
but according to their own version P.W.7 has not given statement, whereas the P.W.5 has deposed police have recorded statement in the police station to the effect that how she has acquainted with the deceased.
Whereas P.W.3 deposed that she has not given any statement before the police.

Whereas the evidence of P.W.4 S.R.Mahesh, Tashildar/Executive Magistrate discloses that on the basis of the requisition received from the Marathahalli police on 27.02.2023 he has conducted inquest Mahazar between 10.30 a.m to 1.00 p.m in the presence of the witnesses C.W.4 to C.W.6 after serving the notice.
The said inquest Mahazar has been marked at Ex.P.7.

In the cross- examination, the way of answer given by the said witness P.W.4 creates lot of doubt because the police informed him to come near C.V.Raman hospital, where he has received the requisition.
The requisition has been marked at Ex.P.9.
The entire history of the case and crime number has written by the police in the requisition.
He has not instructed to write the inquest Mahazar, but he has just told the police about the ligature mark present on the neck region of the deceased.
As such, the police have prepared the inquest Mahazar and thereafter he has signed.
This shows he has just signed the inquest Mahazar prepared by the police as per Ex.P.7.

It appears the police have prepared Ex.P.7 and obtained the signatures of the witnesses including P.W.4.
12.
It is obvious to note that apart from that, the witness P.W.11 Ningapa and P.W12 Shiva being the signatories to the Mahazar marked at Ex.P.15.
The Ex.P.15 reveals that the data present in the mobile was transmitted to the pen drive in the presence of these witnesses by the Investigation Officer with the help of Cyber police.
None of the Cyber police made as witness in the present case.

However, the said witnesses have identified their signatures present on Ex.P.15, but according to the document, the said Mahazar was carried out between 2.00 p.m to 5.30 p.m at C.E.N. police station located at Whitefield.
Whereas in the cross-examination, both the witnesses P.W.11 and P.W.12 have admitted that the police have not issued notice.

It is the say of the witness P.W.11 that he went to the police station at 2.30 p.m, whereas it is the say of P.W.12 he went to the police station at about 1.30 or 2.00 p.m on the say of the police they have signed on the documents.

In their entire evidence,
failed to depose about the transfer of data from the mobile phone of the deceased to the pen drive Ex.P.5 at C.E.N. police station.
According to the version of said witnesses, the said Mahazar has been carried out at Mahadevapura police station.

So, the said witnesses P.W.11 and P.W.12 appears Marathahalli P.S vs A1 Mayukh Mukherjee on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165624995/
4 to be created witnesses just for the purpose of Mahazar Ex.P.15.

sentences.text: The witness P.W.11 admitted that he has never see the video or the list of calls.
As such, the evidence given by the witnesses PW.11 and P.W.12 creates lot of doubt about the conducting of Mahazar Ex.P.15 and their evidence not helpful for the prosecution in any angle.
13. The witness P.W.8 Harish.H.C has traced the accused and produced before the Investigation Officer and submitted report as per Ex.P.12.
The said evidence has completely denied by the accused counsel.
The witness P.W.10 Sobhadeb Ghosh being the advocate well conversant and acquainted with Hindi, English and Bengali language and learnt little Kannada language.
According to him, he has translated the Bengali language into English language on the basis of the available audio clipping and diary.
The document affidavit submitted by him has been marked at Ex.P.14.
He has identified the pen drive already marked at Ex.P.5.
After translation from Bengali to English language sent to SIU Centre, from where he has received the mail.
He has not identified the signature, however according to the said witness, the SIU Centre, after modifying the portion sent to the Investigation Officer.
The said report has been marked at Ex.P.20 and the another document marked at Ex.P.17.
The said evidence has completely denied by the accused counsel.
He has admitted once completion of the translation has to certify whatever the translation carried out is true and thereafter need to be signed.
Whereas on Ex.P.20 no such shara is present.
So, there is a technical error present in the document for its acceptance.
The Investigation Officer could have verified before submitted said documents alongwith charge sheet.

14. It is obvious to note that P.W.13 Anand Marashettar examined by the prosecution has categorically stated before the court on 24.02.2023, when he was discharging the duty of SHO received the information about the suicide of victim by hanging at Plot No.201, situated at 'A' block,
Shradda Palamera Apartment, Kaverappa Layout, Marathahalli, Bengaluru.
Immediately, he visited the spot and informed to the parents of the deceased and sent the dead body to the mortuary of C.V.Raman hospital alongwith requisition through C.W.14.

Thereafter on 26.02.2023 at 4.00 p.m on the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant registered FIR vide Cr.No.47/2023 and sent the FIR Ex.P.16 to the court, on the same day, he has visited the spot and conducted spot Mahazar in the presence of panchas and seized diary and mobile and obtained the signatures of the panchas on the Mahazar.
He has marked the alleged handwriting of the deceased at QD1 to 15 and brought the seized diary into PF and he has recorded statement of C.W.3.
On 27.02.2023 submitted requisition to the C.W.13 to carry out inquest Mahazar on the dead body of the deceased.

The said C.W.13 has carried out inquest Mahazar as per Ex.P.7 in the presence of panchas and thereafter C.W.12 has carried out P.M. as per Ex.P.11 and sent the ligature material used by the deceased to commit suicide.
The said veil marked at M.O.2.
Further he has recorded the statements of the witnesses C.W.4 to C.W.6.
On 01.03.2023 he has sent alongwith panchas C.W.7 and C.W.8 to the Cyber Crime police station, where the data from M.O.1 has been transmitted to the pen-drive Ex.P.5.
Accordingly prepared Mahazar at Ex.P.15.

They brought the pen-drive Ex.P.5 into P.F.No.27/2023 and submitted to the court, on 06.03.2023 he has submitted requisition to the court to send diary and Ex.P.5 i.e. pen-drive to the translator to translate from Bengali to Kannada version.
On 11.03.2023, sent the said diary and pen-drive to the SIU translation Centre alongwith requisition Ex.P.18.
On 14.03.2018 submitted requisition to send the said diary and pen-drive to FSL.
Thereafter handed over further investigation to Shilpa Kamble i.e. P.W.14 W.PSI.

sentences.text: The said witness P.W.14, whose name is not cited in the charge sheet has appeared before the court and deposed that on 30.03.2023 on behalf of the father of the deceased his friend Prabhat Kumar Rat produced the note book consisting of handwriting of the deceased.
The same was seized in the presence of panchas and marked some portion at SD1 to SD5.
Accordingly, prepared Mahazar as per Ex.P.6.
The said note book has been marked at Ex.P.21.

The said Prabath Kumar Ratt i.e.
P.W.2 has produced marriage invitation Ex.P.3 and photos Ex.P.4.
On 03.04.2023 and 05.04.2023 sent the M.O.1 mobile and Ex.P.5 respectively to the FSL and collected the endorsement.
On 11.03.2023, received Ex.P.20 wherein the Bengali language has translated into English and as the investigation was completed, submitted charge sheet against the accused.
This witness P.W.14 has admitted in the cross-examination of accused counsel that in Ex.P.20 name of Puneeth has been referred, but in the investigation she does not know who is this Puneeth.
The other evidence given by PW.13 and P.W.14 has completely denied by the learned counsel for the accused.
In this case, the Investigation Officer P.W.13 before sending the diary Ex.P.17 and pen drive Ex.P.5 to the FSL has sent the same to the SIU Translator Centre.
So, there is clear lapses on the part of the Investigation Officer in carrying out the investigation.
Apart from the evidence of the Investigation Officer, none of the independent witnesses including the father of the deceased failed to support the story of the prosecution.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has completely failed to prove the allegations made against the accused as alleged against him.
As such, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
16. Point No.3:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
The M.O.1 Mobile is released to the interim custody of the father of the deceased.
The M.O.2 Veil being worthless, are ordered to be destroyed after appeal period is over.
Issue intimation to the Jail Authority to release the accused forthwith, if he is not required in any other case.
